## A fourth instance, and this one is the filer's own — written into a dispatch in the same breath as the warning against it

Same seat, 2026-09-19T11:27Z. Recorded here rather than left in a card thread, because it is the strongest
evidence this card has and it is evidence against the seat that filed it.

### The instance

objectui#9928's body cites the spec's positive `limit` declaration at
`packages/spec/src/ui/page.zod.ts:234`. This seat **copied that address into the dispatch brief**
it wrote for that card. Measured afterwards by the dev and re-verified by this seat:

| reading <sub>both rows read 2026-09-19T11:27Z</sub> | value |
|:--|:--|
| `packages/spec` in objectstack-ai/objectui | ⛔ **does not exist** — the spec arrives as the dependency `@objectstack/spec` |
| line 234 of `packages/spec/src/ui/page.zod.ts` in `@objectstack/spec@17.4.0` | a **docblock about RETIRED component types** (`element:filter` / `element:form`) |
| the declaration itself, verified BY CONTENT | **real** — `limit: z.number().int().positive()`, in `component.zod.ts` |

⇒ wrong twice over: wrong repo and wrong line. The claim it carried was true; only the pointer was
false — which is this card's whole thesis.

### ⭐ Why this instance matters more than the other three

The same brief that carried this address also told the dev, verbatim:

> ⚠️ Re-take that address before citing it: this family has already shipped one `file:line` written
> from memory that turned out to point at the wrong docblock.

⇒ the seat wrote the warning and committed the offence **in the same document**. That is not
carelessness about the rule — it is the rule being **unenforceable by attention**. A discipline that
fails while its author is actively reciting it is a discipline that needs a carrier other than
habit, which is direction 1 in this card's list and the reason it was listed last.

⇒ the running count on cards this seat touched in one shift is **four for four**:
objectui#5950 (stale before the branch existed), objectui#8426 (`:704` / `:545` → `:735` / `:579`),
objectui#9899 (`component.zod.ts:2842`, caught by the triage seat that wrote it), and this one.

⚠️ Still ⛔ not a population estimate — four cards this seat happened to work, not a sample of the
board. ⭐ But the failure rate on the cards actually read is the number that matters for whether the
class is worth mechanizing, and it is 4/4.
